profile.scope: Optional aggregate CPU elapsed intervals; scheduling waits may be included. Ready retrieval, exact pixel validation, texture creation and trimming are separate. Request-to-ready latency includes worker decode, polling and main-thread scheduling; it is not pure decode CPU time. Texture creation includes driver work, not GPU execution. Reset excludes request latency for requests already pending. Five fixed stage keys, at most two pending timestamps, no sample history.

profile.scope: Ignored worker experiment. Eight fixed main-thread CPU interval keys; pixel_validation is detached byte-copy work, not the hash. Worker hash elapsed is separately observed and may include descheduling; never sum it into a frame or subtract it as a speedup. Texture creation includes driver submission, not GPU execution. Normal collection polls then joins completed tasks only; final teardown may wait. Source Image and exact-byte reconstruction remain main-thread. No sample history.

profile.scope: Optional aggregate CPU elapsed intervals; scheduling waits may be included. Ready retrieval, exact pixel validation, texture creation and trimming are separate. Request-to-ready latency includes worker decode, polling and main-thread scheduling; it is not pure decode CPU time. Texture creation includes driver work, not GPU execution. Reset excludes request latency for requests already pending. Five fixed stage keys, at most two pending timestamps, no sample history.

scope: Real native ResourceLoader and ImageTexture, exact predecessor vs isolated worker-hash prototype. Four views include full and cropped single-tile admission to expose extra polling latency. Worker elapsed intervals are recorded separately; they can overlap main-thread work and must not be added to it or described as GPU time. Only main-thread whole-pump calls and their nested stages form the submission measurements. Two warmup plus six measured fresh streams per view; sequential fully closed arms alternate and reversed process is separate. OS cache is uncontrolled; no cold-disk claim. One pump per process frame, whole call and nested stage clocks; stage sums are not an additive frame breakdown.
